key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, reaching a roughly €3.53 million net present cost with far fewer simulations than tested black-box baselines.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports integrated sizing of eight energy technologies, including photovoltaics, rather than optimizing solar cells themselves.
method: Propose configuration changes using simulation history and structured memory.
Evaluate designs with year-long simulations and a 25-year net present cost objective.
Keep improvements, automatically revert unsuccessful changes via git, and log every decision.
evidence_signal: On one measured-load building case, three LLM variants ran 10 trials of 50 simulations each; median time to within 1% of the best design was 18–27.5 simulations, versus 192 among successful evolution-strategy trials.
watch_item: Results come from a single building case, and reliability varies by model; broader validation and LLM operating-cost assessment remain important.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
